fields.summary: [mobile] Messaging delivery for opportunities with a learn app
fields.description:
## Overview

For PersonalID messaging opportunities, after finishing learning and claiming, the worker lands on Delivery Home, whose main button opens their PersonalID messaging channel instead of downloading or launching a CommCare deliver app. Tasks that need an app show "No action found for the task", and pending tasks disable the button. Depends on the delivery type/launch slug and null-safety tickets.

## Implementation

From the mobile spec for PersonalID messaging delivery opportunities (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md`):

**Screens**

* Learn progress (`ConnectLearningProgressFragment`, `ConnectLearnCompleteView`): For Messaging opportunities, Claim success always navigates to Delivery Home; never launches a deliver app. The learn-complete CTA uses the "go to delivery" label, never the download-app label.
* Delivery Home (`ConnectDeliveryHomeFragment`): CTA opens messaging (see **Messaging CTA**). No deliver-app install checks. `loadLearningProgress` runs as today (skipped without a learn app via the learn progress API guard).
* Delivery dashboard / more: Task open handled as in **Tasks**. "Revisit learning" shown as today.

**Messaging CTA**

* Opens messaging through `ConnectNavHelper.unlockAndGoToMessaging` with the job's `launchSlug`, matching how conversation tasks open their channel.
* Empty channel id → opens the messaging channel list.
* Consent is handled by the existing channel screen (`ConnectMessageFragment`); no change.

**Tasks**
PersonalID messaging jobs can have pending tasks. Opening one goes through `ConnectTaskPresenter.open` from the dashboard and More tabs:

* **Conversation task**: unchanged. Opens messaging on the task's channel.
* **Any other task**: shows an error toast when there is no app present - "No action found for the task".

**Delivery Home CTA**
Today the CTA is disabled only when the deliver app is installed **and** at least one task is pending. Otherwise it is enabled.

For PersonalID messaging jobs, the messaging CTA counts as an installed deliver app: **the CTA is disabled while any task is pending, and enabled otherwise.** Accepted risk: a pending non-conversation task blocks the CTA, and tapping it only shows the toast, so the worker stays blocked until the server clears the task.

**Job list ordering**

* `lastWorkedDate` is set to now when the user taps the messaging Delivery Home CTA.

**Other**

* Robolectric UI tests for learn-complete claim → Delivery Home and the messaging CTA.
* Update `docs/connect/` with a short note on the PersonalID messaging delivery type.

## Acceptance Criteria

* \[ \] Learn-complete claim on a PersonalID messaging opportunity navigates to Delivery Home and never starts a deliver app download
* \[ \] Learn-complete CTA shows the "go to delivery" label for these opportunities
* \[ \] Delivery Home CTA opens the `launchSlug` channel, or the channel list when the slug is empty, and updates `lastWorkedDate`
* \[ \] Non-conversation tasks show "No action found for the task"; conversation tasks open their channel
* \[ \] Delivery Home CTA is disabled while any task is pending
* \[ \] No deliver-app code path runs for PersonalID messaging opportunities
* \[ \] Robolectric tests and `docs/connect/` note added

## Overview
Each section of the Connect job list shows the opportunity the worker most recently worked on first. This applies to all opportunities, not only PersonalID messaging ones.

## Implementation
Record the time a worker last taps any learn or delivery button (start learning, continue learning, claim, go to delivery, revisit learning, open a task) on an opportunity, keep it across syncs, and sort each job list section by it, newest first. Logging into a CommCare app directly no longer affects the order. Also remove the unused app-installed checks from the job list.

Spec: [Job list ordering](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#job-list-ordering), [Screens](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#screens)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each job list section is ordered by last worked time, most recent first
- Tapping a learn or delivery button, or a task, moves that opportunity to the top of its section
- The order survives an opportunity sync

## Overview
When the app opens messaging for a specific channel that hasn't synced to the device yet (for example, right after claiming, or from a conversation task), the worker stays on the channel list and sees a "Channel doesn't exist" toast instead of the app crashing.

## Implementation
When messaging is asked to open a channel, check that the channel exists on the device first. If it does, open it as today; if not, stay on the channel list and show the toast. This covers both the new messaging button and existing conversation tasks.

Spec: [Messaging CTA](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#messaging-cta)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Opening a channel that isn't on the device shows the channel list and a "Channel doesn't exist" toast, with no crash
- Opening a channel that is on the device still opens it

## Overview
The app reads and stores two new opportunity fields from the server: the delivery type, which marks opportunities delivered through PersonalID messaging, and the launch slug, which is the messaging channel those opportunities open. Nothing uses them yet.

## Implementation
Parse both fields from the opportunity API and save them with the opportunity, using a single Connect database upgrade. Opportunities from older servers, and ones already on the device, default to the existing learn/deliver type with no channel.

Spec: [Server contract](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#server-contract), [Data model and storage](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#data-model-and-storage)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Delivery type and launch slug are saved with each opportunity
- Existing opportunities keep working after the app upgrade and get the defaults
- The database upgrade is covered by a test

## Overview
Opportunities delivered through PersonalID messaging (never a deliver app, learn app optional) sync, are stored, get the right status, and show in the job list without crashing.

## Implementation
- Accept a missing learn app and require no deliver app for PersonalID messaging opportunities; skip any other opportunity whose apps are missing as malformed.
- Keep stored app and learning-module data in line with what the server sends, including removing a learn app the server has dropped.
- A claimed PersonalID messaging opportunity is always in delivery, even on a fresh install or a second device.
- Never request learning progress for an opportunity without a learn app.
- Job list cards fall back to the opportunity's own description and organization.
- Notifications that point at a missing app are dropped.

Spec: [Data model and storage](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#data-model-and-storage), [Opportunity Status](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#opportunity-status), [Learn progress API guard](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#learn-progress-api-guard), [Notifications](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#notifications)

## Acceptance Criteria
- PersonalID messaging opportunities, with and without a learn app, sync and show in the job list without crashing
- Malformed opportunities are skipped
- Claimed PersonalID messaging opportunities show as in delivery after any sync
- No learning progress request for opportunities without a learn app
- Notifications for a missing app are dropped without a crash

## Overview
For PersonalID messaging opportunities, after finishing learning and claiming, the worker lands on Delivery Home, whose main button opens their PersonalID messaging channel instead of downloading or launching a CommCare deliver app. Depends on CCCT-2996 and CCCT-2997.

## Implementation
- After claiming from the learning-complete screen, go straight to Delivery Home; the button reads "go to delivery", never "download app".
- Delivery Home's main button opens the opportunity's messaging channel, or the channel list when none is set.
- Tasks: conversation tasks open their channel as today; any other task shows "No action found for the task". The main button stays disabled while any task is pending.
- Nothing in the delivery screens tries to install or launch a deliver app.
- Add UI tests and a short note to the Connect docs.

Spec: [Screens](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#screens), [Messaging CTA](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#messaging-cta), [Tasks](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#tasks), [Delivery Home CTA](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#delivery-home-cta)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Claiming after learning lands on Delivery Home with no deliver app download
- Delivery Home's button opens the opportunity's messaging channel
- Non-conversation tasks show "No action found for the task"; the button is disabled while tasks are pending
- UI tests and docs note added

## Overview
For PersonalID messaging opportunities with no learn app, the worker reads the Intro page, claims directly from it, and lands on Delivery Home with the messaging button. Learning content is never shown. Depends on CCCT-2997 and CCCT-2998.

## Implementation
- Intro hides the learning cards and its button claims the opportunity, with loading and error states, then opens Delivery Home.
- Opening an unclaimed opportunity of this kind always goes to Intro, never the learning screen.
- "Revisit learning" is hidden on the delivery screens.
- Add a UI test for claiming from Intro.

- Claiming from Intro lands on Delivery Home
- Learning screens and "Revisit learning" are never shown
- UI test added

fields.summary: [mobile] Sort Connect job list by last worked date
fields.description:
## Overview

Each section of the Connect job list shows the opportunity the worker most recently worked on first. This applies to all opportunities, not only PersonalID messaging ones.

## Implementation

Record the time a worker last taps any learn or delivery button (start learning, continue learning, claim, go to delivery, revisit learning, open a task) on an opportunity, keep it across syncs, and sort each job list section by it, newest first. Logging into a CommCare app directly no longer affects the order. Also remove the unused app-installed checks from the job list.

Spec: [Job list ordering](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#job-list-ordering), [Screens](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#screens)

## Acceptance Criteria

* Each job list section is ordered by last worked time, most recent first
* Tapping a learn or delivery button, or a task, moves that opportunity to the top of its section
* The order survives an opportunity sync

When the app opens messaging for a specific channel that hasn't synced to the device yet (for example, right after claiming, or from a conversation task), the worker stays on the channel list and sees a "Channel doesn't exist" toast instead of the app crashing.

When messaging is asked to open a channel, check that the channel exists on the device first. If it does, open it as today; if not, stay on the channel list and show the toast. This covers both the new messaging button and existing conversation tasks.

## Acceptance Criteria

* Opening a channel that isn't on the device shows the channel list and a "Channel doesn't exist" toast, with no crash
* Opening a channel that is on the device still opens it

{"issues":{"nodes":[{"expand":"renderedFields,names,schema,operations,editmeta,changelog,versionedRepresentations","id":"296178","key":"CCCT-2996","fields":{"summary":"[mobile] Store delivery type and launch slug on Connect opportunities","issuetype":{"id":"10005","description":"","iconUrl":"https://jira-prod-us-42-3.prod.atl-paas.net/rest/api/2/universal_avatar/view/type/issuetype/avatar/11046?size=medium","name":"Task","subtask":false,"avatarId":11046,"hierarchyLevel":0},"components":[{"id":"11025","name":"Mobile","description":"Mobile Work for CCC"}],"created":"2026-10-28T02:56:59.613-0400","description":"## Overview

The app reads and stores two new opportunity fields from the server: the delivery type, which marks opportunities delivered through PersonalID messaging, and the launch slug, which is the messaging channel those opportunities open. Nothing uses them yet.

## Implementation

Parse both fields from the opportunity API and save them with the opportunity, using a single Connect database upgrade. Opportunities from older servers, and ones already on the device, default to the existing learn/deliver type with no channel.

Spec: [Server contract](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#server-contract), [Data model and storage](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#data-model-and-storage)

## Acceptance Criteria

* Delivery type and launch slug are saved with each opportunity
* Existing opportunities keep working after the app upgrade and get the defaults
* The database upgrade is covered by a test

fields.summary: [mobile] Store delivery type and launch slug on Connect opportunities
fields.description:
## Overview

The app reads and stores two new opportunity fields from the server: the delivery type, which marks opportunities delivered through PersonalID messaging, and the launch slug, which is the messaging channel those opportunities open. Nothing uses them yet.

## Implementation

Parse both fields from the opportunity API and save them with the opportunity, using a single Connect database upgrade. Opportunities from older servers, and ones already on the device, default to the existing learn/deliver type with no channel.

Spec: [Server contract](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#server-contract), [Data model and storage](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#data-model-and-storage)

## Acceptance Criteria

* Delivery type and launch slug are saved with each opportunity
* Existing opportunities keep working after the app upgrade and get the defaults
* The database upgrade is covered by a test

{"issues":{"nodes":[{"expand":"renderedFields,names,schema,operations,editmeta,changelog,versionedRepresentations","id":"296180","key":"CCCT-2998","fields":{"summary":"[mobile] Messaging delivery for opportunities with a learn app","issuetype":{"id":"10005","description":"","iconUrl":"https://jira-prod-us-42-3.prod.atl-paas.net/rest/api/2/universal_avatar/view/type/issuetype/avatar/11046?size=medium","name":"Task","subtask":false,"avatarId":11046,"hierarchyLevel":0},"components":[{"id":"11025","name":"Mobile","description":"Mobile Work for CCC"}],"created":"2026-10-28T02:57:04.810-0400","description":"## Overview

For PersonalID messaging opportunities, after finishing learning and claiming, the worker lands on Delivery Home, whose main button opens their PersonalID messaging channel instead of downloading or launching a CommCare deliver app. Depends on CCCT-2996 and CCCT-2997.

## Implementation

* After claiming from the learning-complete screen, go straight to Delivery Home; the button reads "go to delivery", never "download app".
* Delivery Home's main button opens the opportunity's messaging channel, or the channel list when none is set.
* Tasks: conversation tasks open their channel as today; any other task shows "No action found for the task". The main button stays disabled while any task is pending.
* Nothing in the delivery screens tries to install or launch a deliver app.
* Add UI tests and a short note to the Connect docs.

Spec: [Screens](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#screens), [Messaging CTA](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#messaging-cta), [Tasks](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#tasks), [Delivery Home CTA](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#delivery-home-cta)

## Acceptance Criteria

* Claiming after learning lands on Delivery Home with no deliver app download
* Delivery Home's button opens the opportunity's messaging channel
* Non-conversation tasks show "No action found for the task"; the button is disabled while tasks are pending
* UI tests and docs note added

fields.description:
## Overview

For PersonalID messaging opportunities, after finishing learning and claiming, the worker lands on Delivery Home, whose main button opens their PersonalID messaging channel instead of downloading or launching a CommCare deliver app. Depends on CCCT-2996 and CCCT-2997.

## Implementation

* After claiming from the learning-complete screen, go straight to Delivery Home; the button reads "go to delivery", never "download app".
* Delivery Home's main button opens the opportunity's messaging channel, or the channel list when none is set.
* Tasks: conversation tasks open their channel as today; any other task shows "No action found for the task". The main button stays disabled while any task is pending.
* Nothing in the delivery screens tries to install or launch a deliver app.
* Add UI tests and a short note to the Connect docs.

Spec: [Screens](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#screens), [Messaging CTA](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#messaging-cta), [Tasks](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#tasks), [Delivery Home CTA](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#delivery-home-cta)

## Acceptance Criteria

* Claiming after learning lands on Delivery Home with no deliver app download
* Delivery Home's button opens the opportunity's messaging channel
* Non-conversation tasks show "No action found for the task"; the button is disabled while tasks are pending
* UI tests and docs note added

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

<tools-used-before-summary>Agent, Bash, Edit, Read, ToolSearch, Write, mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian_MCP__authenticate, mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian_MCP__createJiraIssue, mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian_MCP__editJiraIssue, mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian_MCP__getJiraIssue, mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian_MCP__searchJiraIssuesUsingJql</tools-used-before-summary>
Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - The user started with `/superpowers:brainstorming` to work out what CommCare Android (Connect) would need to change to make the learn app optional on mobile.
   - **The new opportunity type:** opportunities whose delivery happens through PersonalID messaging.
     - `delivery_type = "personalid_messaging"`.
     - `deliver_app` is always null. `learn_app` may or may not be present, and both cases must be supported.
     - The Delivery Home CTA opens PersonalID messaging on the channel given by `launch.slug`. That value is stored on the device as `launchSlug` / `launch_slug`.
   - **Brainstorming result:** a design spec at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md`. The user committed it as `c32ee32ad8` on branch `ccct_2964_ocs_based_opps`, and it is pushed to `origin/ccct_2964_ocs_based_opps`.
   - **Jira tickets:** the user then ran `/jira-tickets-from-plan` on the spec to break it into Jira tickets.
     - Parent CCCT-2860.
     - Component Mobile.
     - Team "Connect: Mobile Team".
     - Sprint "Mobile Team - Sprint 102".
     - Each ticket has a short functional description, and the breakdown was checked for gaps.
   - **Later ticket requests:**
     - Prefix every title with "[mobile]".
     - Rewrite every description: remove implementation details, give a short summary plus a high-level implementation summary that doesn't reference code, and link to the spec sections on GitHub at https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **`ConnectJobRecord`**
     - Status is worked out on the device in `fromJson`; the server's status is not used.
     - `STATUS_AVAILABLE_NEW`/`AVAILABLE`/`LEARNING`/`DELIVERING`.
     - `JobStoreManager.storeOrUpdateJob` never lets a stored status go backwards, and marks newly seen jobs as `AVAILABLE_NEW`.
   - **`ConnectAppRecord`** holds learn/deliver app info. Learn modules exist only inside `learn_app.learn_modules`. `ConnectJobUtils.populateJobs` attaches every stored app record that matches the job UUID.
   - **Connect DB:** `DB_VERSION_CONNECT` = 30. Migrations use versioned snapshot classes (`ConnectJobRecordV2…V21`). Per a memory note, earlier migrations must be retargeted to the new snapshot.
   - **`lastAccessed`:** a local `ConnectLinkedAppRecord` field, set on CommCare app login through `PostLoginSideEffects`. It is used only for job-list sorting, and that sort was ascending.
   - **`lastWorkedDate`:** `ConnectJobRecord` sets it to `new Date()` in the constructor. `fromJson` never reads `last_worked` from the server, and `storeOrUpdateJob` overwrites the stored value on every sync.
   - **Dead install flag:** `ConnectLoginJobListModel.isAppInstalled` is assigned but never read.
   - **Messaging navigation:** `ConnectNavHelper.unlockAndGoToMessaging(activity, policy, channelId, listener)`.
   - **Existing null-channel crash:** `ConnectMessageChannelListFragment.onViewCreated` passes the channel lookup straight to `selectChannel`, which crashes when the channel isn't stored locally.
   - **Tasks:** `ConnectTaskPresenter.open`. A non-conversation task launches the deliver app.
   - **CTA enablement:** `ConnectDeliveryHomeFragment.updateCtaBarEnabled` uses `isCtaEnabled = !appInstalled || !hasPendingTask`.
   - **Jira via the Atlassian MCP:**
     - cloudId `dbff467f-3c3f-4ced-a2ba-a29e1941edd6`.
     - Team field `customfield_10001`; Mobile Team id `1f9ca8ae-dc44-4829-8bcc-39ba3366ca52`.
     - Sprint field `customfield_10010`; sprint 6360 "Mobile Team - Sprint 102" on board 837.
     - Component "Mobile" (id 11025).

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - **`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md`**: the main deliverable. Its sections:
     - Intent, Goals, Server contract.
     - Design:
       - Data model and storage, including the `JobStoreManager` rules for `storeAppInfo` / `storeModules` / `pruneOldJobs`.
       - Opportunity Status: a table of the four places status is set, plus the messaging branch in `fromJson` (claim → DELIVERING; learn app and progress > 0 → LEARNING; otherwise AVAILABLE).
       - Screens table, Job list ordering, Messaging CTA, Tasks, Delivery Home CTA, Learn progress API guard, Notifications, Other.
     - **Local change not in the commit:** the Messaging CTA line was changed to "stays on the channel list and shows a toast, "Channel doesn't exist"". It is a one-line local diff that is not in commit c32ee32.
     - The user also edited the spec directly: they removed the anti-goals and builder's-discretion sections and some "(Our call.)" notes, and changed the `deliver_app` rule to "validate and reject as malformed if not".
   - **Code files read for the investigation** (none were modified):
     - `ConnectJobRecord.java`, `ConnectAppRecord.java`, `JobStoreManager.java`, `ConnectJobUtils.java`.
     - `ConnectOpportunityListFragment.kt`, `ConnectJobIntroFragment.kt`, `ConnectLearningProgressFragment.kt`, `ConnectLearnCompleteView.kt`, `ConnectDeliveryHomeFragment.kt`, `ConnectDeliveryHomeViewModel.kt`.
     - `ConnectDeliveryDashboardFragment.kt`, `ConnectDeliveryMoreFragment.kt`, `BaseConnectFragment.kt`, `ConnectActivity.java`.
     - `ConnectRepository.kt`, `FirebaseMessagingUtil.java`, `ConnectNavHelper.kt`, `ConnectMessageChannelListFragment.java`, `ConnectTaskPresenter.kt`.
     - `PostLoginSideEffects.kt`, `ConnectAppUtils.kt`, `ConnectLinkedAppRecord.java`, `StandardHomeActivityUIController.java`, `NotificationsSyncWorker.kt`, `ConnectDatabaseSchemaManager.kt`.

4. Errors and fixes:

# PersonalID messaging delivery opportunities

## Intent

Connect is adding a new kind of opportunity in which delivery happens through PersonalID messaging
instead of a CommCare deliver app. These opportunities never have a deliver app. They may or may not
have a learn app:

- **With a learn app:** learning works as today. After claiming, the worker goes to Delivery Home,
  whose CTA opens messaging instead of a deliver app.
- **Without a learn app:** the worker reads Intro, claims from Intro, and goes straight to Delivery
  Home with the messaging CTA.

Today the mobile app assumes every opportunity has both apps. Parsing, storage, status derivation,
and most Connect screens dereference `learnAppInfo` / `deliveryAppInfo` unconditionally, so an
opportunity without them either fails to parse or crashes.

## Goals

- Opportunities with `delivery_type = "personalid_messaging"` parse, store, and display without
  crashing, with or without a learn app.
- Without a learn app: job list → Intro → **Claim** on Intro → DELIVERING → Delivery Home with the
  messaging CTA.
- With a learn app: job list → Intro → start learning → learn app → learn progress → claim →
  DELIVERING → Delivery Home with the messaging CTA.
- The status stays DELIVERING across syncs after claim.
- Existing learn/deliver opportunities behave exactly as today, except job list ordering (see
  **Job list ordering**), which changes for all opportunities.


## Server contract

On the opportunity list API, for a PersonalID messaging opportunity:

- `delivery_type`: new string field. `"personalid_messaging"` marks this type. Absent or any other
  value means the existing learn/deliver type (older servers, existing cached jobs).
- `deliver_app`: always `null` when delivery_type is "personalid_messaging".
- `learn_app`: an app object, or `null` when the opportunity has no learn app.
- `learn_progress`: still present; parsed as today but API is only called when learn app is present. 
- `launch.slug`: new nested field holding the messaging channel id the Delivery Home CTA opens.
  `launch` or `slug` would be absent or empty for non PersonalID messaging opportunities.

Other APIs:

- Learn progress API: the client must never call it for a job whose `learnAppInfo` is null.
- Claim API: called from Intro when there is no learn app, and from learn progress (as today) when
  there is one. Without a learn app, the server accepts the claim with no learning completed.
- Delivery progress, deliveries, and payments APIs: unchanged.

## Design

### Data model and storage

- Add a persisted `deliveryType` field to `ConnectJobRecord` (`delivery_type`). Branches use two
  checks on the record:
  - **PersonalID messaging delivery** (`deliveryType == "personalid_messaging"`): governs everything
    on the delivery side (deliver app, Delivery Home CTA, tasks).
  - **Has learn app** (`learnAppInfo != null`): governs everything on the learn side (Intro learn
    cards, start learning vs. claim, learn progress API, revisit learning).
- Add a persisted `launchSlug` field (`launch_slug`), parsed from `launch.slug` (empty when absent).
- Bump `DB_VERSION_CONNECT` (currently 30) once for both new fields, add the `ConnectJobRecordV<N>`
  snapshot, and add an upgrade step in `ConnectDatabaseUpgrader` that backfills existing rows with
  the default type and an empty channel id.
  Prior migrations that targeted `ConnectJobRecord.class` must be retargeted to the new snapshot,
  following the existing V2…V21 pattern.
- `ConnectJobRecord.fromJson`:
  - PersonalID messaging job: `learn_app` is nullable. `deliver_app`
    record is always null, validate and reject as malformed if not. 
  - Any other job: a null or missing `learn_app` or `deliver_app` is rejected as malformed (throws,
    so `ConnectOpportunitiesParser` skips the job as it does other bad entries). This keeps
    learn/deliver paths free of null guards. *(Our call.)*
- `JobStoreManager`. Stored app records and learn modules mirror the server, and no step reads
  fields of an app record that is null:
  - `storeAppInfo`: an app that is present is written as today. When `learnAppInfo` or
    `deliveryAppInfo` is null, any stored record of that kind for the job is deleted and nothing is
    written. Without the delete, `ConnectJobUtils.populateJobs`, which attaches every stored app
    record matching the job UUID, would bring back a learn app the server has removed.
  - `storeModules`: a null `learnAppInfo` counts as an empty incoming module list. The existing
    prune step deletes the job's stored modules, and nothing is written. Modules only arrive inside
    `learn_app.learn_modules`.
  - `pruneOldJobs`: when deleting a job the server no longer sends, it collects IDs only from app
    records that are present. Module IDs come from `learnAppInfo` when it is present. Without a
    learn app the job has no stored modules, because `storeModules` keeps them empty.

### Opportunity Status

Opportunity Status is set locally in four places:

| Where | What it does | PersonalID messaging change |
|---|---|---|
| `ConnectJobRecord.fromJson` | Derives AVAILABLE / LEARNING / DELIVERING from learn progress and `claim`. | New branch, below. |
| `JobStoreManager.storeOrUpdateJob` | Keeps the stored status if it is further along than the parsed one; marks newly seen AVAILABLE jobs AVAILABLE_NEW. | None. |
| `ConnectJobIntroFragment` start-learning success | Sets LEARNING. | Unchanged with a learn app; not reached without one. |
| `ConnectRepository.claimJob` success | Sets DELIVERING. | None; both claim entry points reuse it. |

`fromJson` branch for PersonalID messaging jobs:

1. `claim` present → DELIVERING.
2. Otherwise, has a learn app and learn progress > 0 → LEARNING.
3. Otherwise → AVAILABLE.

Without a learn app the job never enters LEARNING. The claim rule is needed because the
no-regression rule in `storeOrUpdateJob` only protects a device that recorded the claim locally. A
fresh install, a second device, or a claim made outside this device would otherwise derive
AVAILABLE and show Intro for a claimed job.

`passedAssessment()` reads `learnAppInfo.passingScore`, so it must not run for jobs without a learn
app.

### Screens

| Screen | With learn app                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Without learn app |
|---|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---|
| Job list (`ConnectOpportunityListFragment`) | For all jobs: remove the unused `isAppInstalled` checks and the unused `ConnectLoginJobListModel.isAppInstalled` field (nothing reads it), and sort as in **Job list ordering**. No app record lookups remain. | Same. |
| Intro (`ConnectJobIntroFragment`) | As today: learn cards shown, CTA starts learning.                                                                                                                                                              | Learn cards dropped entirely. CTA claims the job, then navigates to Delivery Home. |
| Learn progress (`ConnectLearningProgressFragment`, `ConnectLearnCompleteView`) | For Messaging opportunities, Claim success always navigates to Delivery Home; never launches a deliver app. The learn-complete CTA uses the "go to delivery" label, never the download-app label.              | Not reached. |
| Delivery Home (`ConnectDeliveryHomeFragment`) | CTA opens messaging (see **Messaging CTA**). No deliver-app install checks. `loadLearningProgress` runs as today.                                                                                              | Same, but `loadLearningProgress` is skipped. |
| Delivery dashboard / more | Task open handled as in **Tasks**. "Revisit learning" shown as today.                                                                                                                                          | Task open handled as in **Tasks**. "Revisit learning" hidden. |
| `ConnectActivity.handleInfoRedirect` | As today.                                                                                                                                                                                                      | A non-delivering job routes to Intro, not the learn progress screen. |

For jobs without a learn app, Intro needs claim handling (loading, error, success). It currently
lives only in `ConnectLearningProgressViewModel`, so Intro's ViewModel needs the same handling.

At places where job list cards would read description and organization from an app record, 
we would read them from the job record when app record is absent.

### Job list ordering

Applies to all opportunities, not only PersonalID messaging ones.

- Each job list section sorts by `ConnectJobRecord.lastWorkedDate`, most recent first. This replaces
  the sort by the linked app's `lastAccessed` (`processJobRecords`), which was ascending
  (least recent first) and only updated on CommCare app login.
- `lastWorkedDate` is set to now whenever the user taps a learn or delivery CTA for the job:
  - Intro CTA (start learning, or claim when there is no learn app)
  - Learn progress continue CTA
  - Learn-complete claim CTA
  - Delivery Home CTA (deliver app or messaging)
  - "Revisit learning"
  - Task taps on the dashboard and More tabs
- `last_worked` from the server stays unparsed. `JobStoreManager.storeOrUpdateJob` copies the
  stored `lastWorkedDate` onto the incoming record before writing, the same way it keeps status
  from going backwards. A newly seen job keeps the constructor default (first sync time).
- Logging into a CommCare app directly (not through a Connect CTA) no longer affects ordering.
- `lastWorkedDate` is already persisted; no migration needed for it.

### Messaging CTA

- Opens messaging through `ConnectNavHelper.unlockAndGoToMessaging` with the job's
  `launchSlug`, matching how conversation tasks open their channel.
- Empty channel id → opens the messaging channel list.
- Channel id not yet in the local messaging DB (for example, right after claim, before messages
  sync) → stays on the channel list and shows a toast, "Channel doesn't exist". Today
  `ConnectMessageChannelListFragment.onViewCreated` passes the lookup result straight to
  `selectChannel`, which crashes on null. The fix belongs there, so it also covers conversation
  tasks.
- Consent is handled by the existing channel screen (`ConnectMessageFragment`); no change.

### Tasks

PersonalID messaging jobs can have pending tasks. Opening one goes through
`ConnectTaskPresenter.open` from the dashboard and More tabs:

- **Conversation task** : unchanged. Opens messaging on the task's channel.
- **Any other task**: shows an error toast when there is no app present -  "No action found for the task".

### Delivery Home CTA 

Today the CTA is disabled only when the deliver
app is installed **and** at least one task is pending. Otherwise it is enabled.

For PersonalID messaging jobs, the messaging CTA counts as an installed deliver app: **the CTA is
disabled while any task is pending, and enabled otherwise.** Accepted risk: a pending
non-conversation task blocks the CTA, and tapping it only shows the toast, so the worker stays
blocked until the server clears the task.

### Learn progress API guard

Guard inside `ConnectRepository.getLearningProgress`: if `learnAppInfo` is null, don't make the call.
This covers Delivery Home's `loadLearningProgress` and any future caller.

### Notifications

`ConnectJobUtils.getAppIdForOpportunity` (used by session-endpoint notifications in
`FirebaseMessagingUtil`) returns null when the requested app is absent. `handleSessionEndpointNotification` treats null
like its existing unresolved-app case and returns null, so no notification is shown.

## Other

- Robolectric UI tests for Intro claim → Delivery Home, learn-complete claim → Delivery
  Home, and the messaging CTA.
- Update `docs/connect/` with a short note on the PersonalID messaging delivery type.

116	| Learn progress (`ConnectLearningProgressFragment`, `ConnectLearnCompleteView`) | For Messaging opportunities, Claim success always navigates to Delivery Home; never launches a deliver app. The learn-complete CTA uses the "go to delivery" label, never the download-app label.              | Not reached. |
117	| Delivery Home (`ConnectDeliveryHomeFragment`) | CTA opens messaging (see **Messaging CTA**). No deliver-app install checks. `loadLearningProgress` runs as today.                                                                                              | Same, but `loadLearningProgress` is skipped. |
118	| Delivery dashboard / more | Task open handled as in **Tasks**. "Revisit learning" shown as today.                                                                                                                                          | Task open handled as in **Tasks**. "Revisit learning" hidden. |
119	| `ConnectActivity.handleInfoRedirect` | As today.                                                                                                                                                                                                      | A non-delivering job routes to Intro, not the learn progress screen. |
120	
121	For jobs without a learn app, Intro needs claim handling (loading, error, success). It currently
122	lives only in `ConnectLearningProgressViewModel`, so Intro's ViewModel needs the same handling.
123	
124	At places where job list cards would read description and organization from an app record, 
125	we would read them from the job record when app record is absent.
126	
127	### Job list ordering
128	
129	Applies to all opportunities, not only PersonalID messaging ones.
130	
131	- Each job list section sorts by `ConnectJobRecord.lastWorkedDate`, most recent first. This replaces
132	  the sort by the linked app's `lastAccessed` (`processJobRecords`), which was ascending
133	  (least recent first) and only updated on CommCare app login.
134	- `lastWorkedDate` is set to now whenever the user taps a learn or delivery CTA for the job:
135	  - Intro CTA (start learning, or claim when there is no learn app)
136	  - Learn progress continue CTA
137	  - Learn-complete claim CTA
138	  - Delivery Home CTA (deliver app or messaging)
139	  - "Revisit learning"
140	  - Task taps on the dashboard and More tabs
141	- `last_worked` from the server stays unparsed. `JobStoreManager.storeOrUpdateJob` copies the
142	  stored `lastWorkedDate` onto the incoming record before writing, the same way it keeps status
143	  from going backwards. A newly seen job keeps the constructor default (first sync time).
144	- Logging into a CommCare app directly (not through a Connect CTA) no longer affects ordering.
145	- `lastWorkedDate` is already persisted; no migration needed for it.
146	
147	### Messaging CTA
148	
149	- Opens messaging through `ConnectNavHelper.unlockAndGoToMessaging` with the job's
150	  `launchSlug`, matching how conversation tasks open their channel.
151	- Empty channel id → opens the messaging channel list.
152	- Channel id not yet in the local messaging DB (for example, right after claim, before messages
153	  sync) → stays on the channel list and shows a toast, "Channel doesn't exist". Today
154	  `ConnectMessageChannelListFragment.onViewCreated` passes the lookup result straight to
155	  `selectChannel`, which crashes on null. The fix belongs there, so it also covers conversation
156	  tasks.
157	- Consent is handled by the existing channel screen (`ConnectMessageFragment`); no change.
158	
159	### Tasks
160	
161	PersonalID messaging jobs can have pending tasks. Opening one goes through
162	`ConnectTaskPresenter.open` from the dashboard and More tabs:
163	
164	- **Conversation task** : unchanged. Opens messaging on the task's channel.
165	- **Any other task**: shows an error toast when there is no app present -  "No action found for the task".
166	
167	### Delivery Home CTA 
168	
169	Today the CTA is disabled only when the deliver
170	app is installed **and** at least one task is pending. Otherwise it is enabled.
171	
172	For PersonalID messaging jobs, the messaging CTA counts as an installed deliver app: **the CTA is
173	disabled while any task is pending, and enabled otherwise.** Accepted risk: a pending
174	non-conversation task blocks the CTA, and tapping it only shows the toast, so the worker stays
175	blocked until the server clears the task.
176	
177	### Learn progress API guard
178	
179	Guard inside `ConnectRepository.getLearningProgress`: if `learnAppInfo` is null, don't make the call.
180	This covers Delivery Home's `loadLearningProgress` and any future caller.
181	
182	### Notifications
183	
184	`ConnectJobUtils.getAppIdForOpportunity` (used by session-endpoint notifications in
185	`FirebaseMessagingUtil`) returns null when the requested app is absent. `handleSessionEndpointNotification` treats null
186	like its existing unresolved-app case and returns null, so no notification is shown.
187	
188	## Other
189	
190	- Robolectric UI tests for Intro claim → Delivery Home, learn-complete claim → Delivery
191	  Home, and the messaging CTA.
192	- Update `docs/connect/` with a short note on the PersonalID messaging delivery type.
193	
</system-reminder>

# Jira Tickets from Implementation Plan

## Overview

Reviews an implementation plan, breaks it into logically independent tickets, and creates them in Jira with descriptions, implementation details, and Backlog status. It works best if the plan is supplied as a Github link. 

## Process

### Step 1: Review the Plan

Read the full implementation plan. Identify logical breakpoints using these criteria (in priority order):

1. **Independently deployable** — each ticket can be merged and deployed without depending on other in-progress work
2. **max ~500 lines per PR** — keeps PRs easy to review; split further if a ticket would exceed this

### Step 2: Ask About Custom Fields

Before creating any tickets, ask the user:

> "Would you like to populate additional ticket fields (e.g components)?"

- **No** → proceed to Step 3 with defaults
- **Yes** → ask for each field value one at a time before creating tickets

### Step 3: Confirm Tickets

Present the complete list of tickets to the user and confirm if we are ok to proceed to ticket creation or iterate with additional information from user. 

### Step 4: Create Each Ticket

Use `mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian__createJiraIssue` for each ticket with:

- **Summary**: Clear, action-oriented description of what the ticket targets
- **Description**: Overview of the changes
- **Status**: Backlog
- **Parent**: Keep 'parent' same as the 'parent' of ticket mentioned in plan


## Ticket Description Template

```
## Overview
[1-3 sentences describing what this ticket accomplishes and why]

## Implementation

Link to the relevant section of Github Plan if a Github link is available, otherwise copy the relevant section of implementation plan verbatim here. 

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] [Key outcome that signals this ticket is done]
```

# Brainstorming

You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
anything gets built.

People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.

## First: What Do You Actually Know?

Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
why?

- **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
  blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
- **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.

## Your First Message

Your first message is two things, in this order:

1. One line letting them know that if they'd rather skip the questions and
   have you just start, they can say so. If they take you up on it, this
   skill is done: state any significant how-it-gets-made choice
   (platform, language, medium) in one plain line, then do what they
   asked through the normal workflow.
2. One open question that gets them describing. Ask about a real moment
   or a concrete picture: "What's the moment you find yourself wishing
   this existed?" or "Tell me about the people who'll be in the room."

<system-reminder>
The following skills are available for use with the Skill tool:

- jira-tickets-from-plan: Use when creating Jira tickets from an implementation plan.
- no-ai-slop: Edit drafts into sharper, more human writing while preserving the writer's personal voice, or detect AI-slop patterns without rewriting. Use when the user wants a draft clearer, more direct, more opinionated, or less AI-sounding, or asks whether writing reads as AI.
- summarize-spec (condensing-specs-for-design-review): Produce a short, high-level companion doc alongside a Superpowers design spec (docs/superpowers/specs/*.md) for team design review — before implementation exists. Use whenever a spec is written or about to be sent for team approval, whenever the user says a spec is too long, too verbose, or too full of code references for reviewers to get through, or asks for a condensed/high-level version of a spec. This is distinct from a PR description: there is no diff yet, so this doc must carry the approach itself, not just point at what changed. Do not send the full spec for team approval without also producing this companion doc.
- my-rebase: /dev-utils:git-rebase restructure commits on my branch for a commit by commit review, put any ref...
- dev-utils:review-plan: Interactively review a plan across architecture, code quality, tests, and performance before any code changes.
- open-code-review:delegate-review: Run OCR in delegation mode — OCR handles file selection and rules, the host agent performs the actual review.
- open-code-review:review: Run OpenCodeReview (OCR) to review code changes and autonomously apply fixes.
- code-review:code-review: This skill should be used when the user asks to review code, check a PR, audit a file or module, look at code quality, assess a codebase, or says things like "what do you think of this code", "review my changes", "look at this file", "check this PR", or "does this look right". Trigger on any request to evaluate, critique, or assess code — even casually phrased ones. Performs thorough, senior-engineer-quality code reviews that go beyond bug detection.
- code-review:pair-review: Interactively review a GitHub PR commit by commit, together with the user, in a dedicated `review` worktree. Use this whenever the user drops a PR link and wants to go through it *with* you rather than have it reviewed *for* them — "pair review this PR", "let's review this one together", "walk me through PR 123 commit by commit", or a PR URL plus "review this with me". The user reads the code and writes their own comments in GitHub; you explain what each commit and each line does, answer follow-ups against a real checkout, and read their pending review back to them. Never writes to GitHub. For a hands-off automated review with no user in the loop, use the code-review skill instead.
- commcare-tech:dependency-upgrade: Upgrade a Python or JS dependency safely. Given a library name, finds the latest safe version, reviews the changelog, assesses impact based on how the library is used in the repo, performs the upgrade, and creates a PR with the changelog and assessment. Use this whenever someone asks to upgrade, bump, or update a package/library/dependency.
- commcare-tech:dependency-upgrade-review: Review a Dependabot or other dependency-bump PR — identify the changed packages, research their changelogs, assess breaking-change and codebase impact, and post the analysis as a PR comment. Use this whenever someone asks to review, analyze, or evaluate a dependency-upgrade PR.
- commcare-tech:jira-cve: Create a security ticket in JIRA for a CVE from a GitHub Dependabot alert URL.
- commcare-tech:jira-ticket: Create a SAAS Jira ticket. Just describe what you're working on and it handles the rest.
- commcare-tech:score-deet-week: Use when the user wants to divide up, assign, or distribute unscored Jira tickets from the SAAS deet week board (board 252) for scoring/grooming. Triggers on phrases like "score deet week", "split up the unscored tickets", "divide unscored tickets", "assign tickets for scoring", or "who should score these". Mobile tickets always go to Ahmad; the rest get split evenly among the other Platform devs. Posts the result to Slack
- commcare-tech:writing-commits-and-prs: Use when drafting a commit message, naming a branch, writing a PR title, or composing/editing a PR description in any Dimagi repo. Also use before running `gh pr edit --body` against an existing PR.
- connect-tech:connect-web-release-notes: Generates Markdown release notes for the latest commcare-connect release and posts them to Confluence and Slack. Use when the user asks for Connect release notes, a changelog, or what changed in the last release (no repo URL needed).
- connect-tech:docs-vs-code-review: Reviews Confluence docs against source code to find inaccuracies and suggest fixes. Use when the user provides a Confluence URL and asks to review, audit, or check if docs are accurate or up to date (GitHub repo not required — inferred from the Confluence space).
- connect-tech:groom-sprint-tickets: Slash command: /groom-sprint-tickets <sprint name>. Do NOT auto-invoke. Only runs when explicitly called via slash command.
- connect-tech:jira-bug-ticket: Create a Jira bug ticket. Use when the user asks to file, log, report, or create a bug or defect in Jira ("create a bug ticket", "log a bug", "report a bug", "open a ticket for this bug").
- connect-tech:jira-feature-request: Create Jira feature request tickets (Stories) in the CI project using Dimagi's form 134 format. Use this skill whenever a user wants to submit, log, or create a feature request, new feature idea, product enhancement, or user story in Jira. Triggers on phrases like "create a feature request", "submit a feature idea", "log a feature", "I want to request a feature", "add this to the backlog", "create a story", or any time someone describes something they want the product to do that it doesn't do yet. Always use this skill when feature requests or product enhancements need to be tracked, even if the user doesn't say "Jira" or "ticket" explicitly.
- connect-tech:jira-spec-doc: Generates a product spec doc in Markdown from a Jira ticket. Use when the user provides a Jira ticket ID (e.g. CCC-284) or URL and asks for a spec, design doc, or tech spec ("write a spec for this ticket", "make a spec from this Jira").
- connect-tech:jira-tickets-from-plan: Use when creating Jira tickets from a AI plan.
- connect-tech:release-notes: Generates Markdown release notes for the most recent release of a GitHub repository. Use when the user asks to "generate release notes", "write a changelog", or "summarize the last release" for a GitHub repo (owner/repo or full URL).
- dev-utils:add-mobile-string: Use when the user asks to add a new Android string resource with translations to the CommCare Android project, given a string resource name and English text
- dev-utils:audit-dependencies: Run a full dependency audit for a project — covers Python (pip-tools) and front-end (npm/yarn) if present. Produces report, applies safe bumps, emits Jira-ready ticket list for risky/EoL items. Use when running quarterly maintenance or on demand.
- dev-utils:babysit-prs: One sweep over my open PRs — address new review comments, check CI, branch freshness, lint/format & generated-artifact drift, and description sync, fixing and pushing — tracking state so reruns skip already-handled work. Designed to be driven by /loop. Pass a PR number to work a single PR instead.
- dev-utils:create-mobile-pr: Use when creating, opening, or submitting a pull request in a Dimagi mobile/CommCare repo — identified by JIRA-prefixed branches (e.g. CCCT-1929-...), a `RELEASES.md` with `### Release Notes` and `### QA Notes` sections, and the dimagi PR template (Safety story / Product Description / Technical Summary / QA Plan). Also triggers on "ship this" or when implementation is complete and ready to push. For repos without these conventions, use the generic `create-pr` skill instead.
- dev-utils:create-pr: Use when the user asks to create, open, or submit a GitHub pull request, says "make a PR", "open a PR", or wants to commit, push, and turn the current branch into a PR. For mobile/CommCare repos with JIRA-prefixed tickets and RELEASES.md QA notes, prefer create-mobile-pr instead.
- dev-utils:explain-diff-html: Use when the user asks for a rich explanation of a code change, diff, branch, or PR. Produces HTML output.
- dev-utils:git-rebase: Use when squashing fixup commits into earlier commits, cleaning up a feature branch with interactive rebase, recovering a dropped or failed autosquash, inserting a reformatting commit before code changes, moving file changes between commits, splitting one working-tree edit across several historical commits, or diagnosing autosquash conflicts.
- dev-utils:grill-me: Interview the user relentlessly about a plan or design until reaching shared understanding, resolving each branch of the decision tree. Use when user wants to stress-test a plan, get grilled on their design, or mentions "grill me".
- dev-utils:iterate-pr: Fix CI failures and address review feedback on the current branch's PR. Use when CI is failing, review comments need addressing, or you need to push fixes for an open PR. Supports --dry-run to preview without changes.
- dev-utils:pr-status-report: Use when the user asks for a PR report, PR status, open PRs overview, or wants to know which pull requests need their attention in the current repository
- dev-utils:vertical-ordering: Use when writing new functions, extracting helpers, refactoring modules, or reorganizing code — any time function placement order is a decision
- manager:goals: Conversational skill for reviewing, updating, and refining your professional goals.
- manager:shutdown: End of day wrap-up — captures what got done, what didn't, and plans for tomorrow. Weekly close-out on configurable review day (default Friday).
- manager:standup: Morning check-in — surfaces goals, summarizes where you left off, captures today's plan, and gives goal-alignment feedback. Weekly review mode on configurable review day (default Friday).
- manager:sync: Prep for 1:1s with your manager — auto-summarizes journal entries since your last sync into a briefing with wins, progress, and blockers.
- superpowers:brainstorming: You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, modifying behavior, or planning anything new, in software or out of it (a talk, a business, a renovation).
- superpowers:diagnosing-superpowers: Use when a superpowers session went wrong and your human partner wants to know why — repeated work, ignored plans, stumbles, poor results, a skill that didn't fire, "it took too long", "why is it so expensive", "what is it doing" — or wants to build a bug report for the superpowers maintainers, for the current session or a past one identified by id or path, on any harness.
- superpowers:dispatching-parallel-agents: Use when facing 2+ independent tasks that can be worked on without shared state or sequential dependencies
- superpowers:executing-plans: Use when executing an implementation plan in the current session as the implementer yourself — your human partner chose inline execution, or no subagent tool is available
- superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch: Use when implementation is complete, all tests pass, and you need to decide how to integrate the work
- superpowers:receiving-code-review: Use when receiving code review feedback, before implementing suggestions, especially if feedback seems unclear or technically questionable - requires technical rigor and verification, not performative agreement or blind implementation
- superpowers:requesting-code-review: Use when completing tasks, implementing major features, or before merging to verify work meets requirements
- superpowers:subagent-driven-development: Use when executing implementation plans with independent tasks in the current session
- superpowers:systematic-debugging: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes
- superpowers:test-driven-development: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code
- superpowers:using-git-worktrees: Use when starting feature work that needs isolation from current workspace or before executing implementation plans - ensures an isolated workspace exists via native tools or git worktree fallback
- superpowers:using-superpowers: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring skill invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions
- superpowers:verification-before-completion: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always
- superpowers:writing-plans: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code
- superpowers:writing-skills: Use when creating new skills, editing existing skills, or verifying skills work before deployment
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, handing the viewer a file to save, or using the viewer's camera, microphone, location, screen or device motion. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- plugin-authoring: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a panel or pane that stays beside the chat and updates, a band, status line, toast, slash command, or hook on tool calls. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- anthropic-skills:built-in-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.
- anthropic-skills:chrome-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.
- anthropic-skills:computer-use: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills.
- anthropic-skills:deep-research: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly.
- anthropic-skills:docs: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:google-workspace: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.
- anthropic-skills:import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:summarizing-specs-for-review
- anthropic-skills:xlsx
</system-reminder>
