description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. schema.name: SendFeedback
schema.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. - Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

content.text:
Today each section of the job list is sorted by the linked CommCare app's `lastAccessed`, oldest first, so the opportunity you used least recently is at the top. [Certain] The code is in `app/src/org/commcare/fragments/connect/ConnectOpportunityListFragment.kt:176-183`.

**How it works:**
- There are three sections: In progress, New and Finished. Each one is sorted with `sortBy { it.lastAccessed }`, which is ascending.
- In progress: completed-delivery jobs are sorted separately and added at the end.
- The sort value comes from `processJobRecords` (line 233). It finds the job's app (the learn app for learning rows, the deliver app for delivery, new and finished rows) and reads that app's `ConnectLinkedAppRecord.lastAccessed`.
- That value is only written in two places:
  - When the linked app record is first created (`ConnectLinkedAppRecord.java:75`).
  - On CommCare app login (`PostLoginSideEffects.kt:42` → `ConnectAppUtils.updateLastAccessed`).
- If the app has no linked record (never installed or logged into), it uses `Date()`, the time the list was built. Those jobs end up at the bottom, below every job that has a record. Among themselves they come out in the order they were processed, because the timestamps are all nearly the same.

**What this means:**
- **New:** most new jobs have no linked record, so this section is effectively in database order.
- **In progress:** sorted by when you last logged into the learn or deliver app, oldest first.

The spec's **Job list ordering** section matches this: it replaces the sort with `lastWorkedDate`, most recent first.

content.text:
No, there's no sync triggered because the channel is missing. Today the app crashes before any sync can start. [Certain]

**What happens today** (`app/src/org/commcare/fragments/connectMessaging/ConnectMessageChannelListFragment.java`):
1. `goToMessaging` opens `ConnectMessagingActivity` with the channel id and does no lookup or sync of its own (`ConnectNavHelper.kt:55`).
2. `onViewCreated` (line 76) looks the channel up in the local DB only. When it isn't found, `getMessagingChannel` returns null, and `selectChannel(null)` calls `channel.getChannelId()`, which throws a NullPointerException.
3. A full message sync, `MessageManager.retrieveMessages`, runs in `onResume` (line 98) on every visit to the channel list. But `onResume` comes after `onViewCreated`, so in the missing-channel case it never gets that far.

**With the fix in the spec (toast, stay on the list):** the screen survives, so the `onResume` sync now runs and `refreshUi` adds the new channel to the list. [Certain] That sync is the normal one every list visit does, not one triggered by the missing channel.

**Gap in the spec:** the lookup happens before the sync, so right after a claim (the exact case the spec describes) the worker would see "Channel doesn't exist". A second later the channel shows up in the list, but it doesn't open on its own. The toast would be wrong at that point and the worker would have to tap the channel.

What I'd do instead: when the channel isn't found locally, wait for the `retrieveMessages` result, then look the channel up again. Open it if it's there now, and show "Channel doesn't exist" only if it's still missing (or the sync failed). This is a small change in the same fragment and covers conversation tasks as well. Do you want me to update the Messaging CTA section of the spec and the CCCT-2995 description to match?

fields.description:
## Overview

When the app opens messaging for a specific channel that hasn't synced to the device yet (for example, right after claiming, or from a conversation task), it fetches the latest messages and opens the channel once it arrives. If the channel still doesn't exist, the worker stays on the channel list and sees a "Channel doesn't exist" toast instead of the app crashing.

## Implementation

When messaging is asked to open a channel, check whether the channel exists on the device. If it does, open it as today. If not, stay on the channel list, wait for the messages sync to finish, and check again: open the channel if it now exists, otherwise show the toast. This covers both the new messaging button and existing conversation tasks.

Spec: [Messaging CTA](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#messaging-cta)

## Acceptance Criteria

* Opening a channel that isn't on the device but arrives in the messages sync opens that channel
* Opening a channel that is still missing after the sync, or when the sync fails, shows the channel list and a "Channel doesn't exist" toast, with no crash
* Opening a channel that is on the device still opens it

fields.description:
## Overview

When the app opens messaging for a specific channel that hasn't synced to the device yet (for example, right after claiming, or from a conversation task), it fetches the latest messages and opens the channel once it arrives. If the channel still doesn't exist, the worker stays on the channel list and sees a "Channel doesn't exist" toast instead of the app crashing.

## Implementation

When messaging is asked to open a channel, check whether the channel exists on the device. If it does, open it as today. If not, stay on the channel list, wait for the messages sync to finish, and check again: open the channel if it now exists, otherwise show the toast. This covers both the new messaging button and existing conversation tasks.

Spec: [Messaging CTA](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#messaging-cta)

## Acceptance Criteria

* Opening a channel that isn't on the device but arrives in the messages sync opens that channel
* Opening a channel that is still missing after the sync, or when the sync fails, shows the channel list and a "Channel doesn't exist" toast, with no crash
* Opening a channel that is on the device still opens it

content.text:
I've updated both the spec and CCCT-2995. The ticket's "Messaging CTA" link still points to commit `c32ee32`, which has neither this change nor the earlier toast change. [Certain] The spec edits are only in your local copy.

**Spec** (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md`, Messaging CTA section): when the channel isn't on the device, the app now stays on the channel list and waits for the messages sync (`MessageManager.retrieveMessages`) to finish. Then it looks the channel up again. It opens the channel if it's there now, and shows "Channel doesn't exist" if it's still missing or the sync failed. The section also notes that today the lookup runs in `onViewCreated`, before the `onResume` sync.

**CCCT-2995:** the overview, implementation summary and acceptance criteria now describe the same flow. There are three acceptance criteria:
- A channel that arrives in the sync opens.
- A channel that's still missing, or a failed sync, shows the toast with no crash.
- A channel already on the device still opens.

I haven't committed anything. Once you commit and push the spec, I can update the links in all six tickets to the new commit.

content.text:
No, null learn and deliver apps don't need a DB update. [Certain]

**Why:**
- `learnAppInfo` and `deliveryAppInfo` on `ConnectJobRecord` (`ConnectJobRecord.java:183-184`) aren't persisted columns. They have no `@Persisting` annotation and are transient fields.
- Each app is stored as its own row in the `ConnectAppRecord` table. Those rows are keyed by job UUID and have an `isLearning` flag (`ConnectAppRecord.java:35-67`).
- When a job is loaded, `ConnectJobUtils.populateJobs` attaches whichever rows match the job.
- So "no learn app" just means there's no learn row for that job. The schema already supports this.

**What does need handling** is the storage code, and **CCCT-2997** covers it (spec section *Data model and storage*, the `JobStoreManager` rules):
- `storeAppInfo` deletes the stored row of that kind when the app is null, so `populateJobs` can't bring back a stale learn app.
- `storeModules` treats a null learn app as an empty module list.
- `pruneOldJobs` skips null apps when it collects IDs to delete.

The only DB migration in this work is in **CCCT-2996**: the `DB_VERSION_CONNECT` bump that adds the `deliveryType` and `launchSlug` columns to `ConnectJobRecord`.

input.old_string:
- `last_worked` from the server stays unparsed. `JobStoreManager.storeOrUpdateJob` copies the
  stored `lastWorkedDate` onto the incoming record before writing, the same way it keeps status
  from going backwards. A newly seen job keeps the constructor default (first sync time).
input.new_string:
- `ConnectJobRecord.fromJson` sets `lastWorkedDate` from the server's `last_active`. When
  `last_active` is absent or null (older servers, never-worked jobs), it is set to the epoch, not
  the constructor default of now, so a never-worked job does not outrank worked ones and the
  server value is not masked on a fresh install.
- `JobStoreManager.storeOrUpdateJob` keeps the more recent of the stored and incoming
  `lastWorkedDate`, the same way it keeps status from going backwards. A local CTA tap is kept
  until the server reports a later time; on a fresh install or second device the server value
  restores the order.
- Accepted risk: local values come from the device clock and server values from the server clock,
  so a device with a wrong clock can order jobs incorrectly.

{"issues":{"nodes":[{"expand":"renderedFields,names,schema,operations,editmeta,changelog,versionedRepresentations","id":"296176","key":"CCCT-2994","fields":{"summary":"[mobile] Sort Connect job list by last worked date","issuetype":{"id":"10009","description":"Stories track functionality or features expressed as user goals.","iconUrl":"https://jira-prod-us-42-3.prod.atl-paas.net/rest/api/2/universal_avatar/view/type/issuetype/avatar/10315?size=medium","name":"Story","subtask":false,"avatarId":10315,"hierarchyLevel":0},"components":[{"id":"11025","name":"Mobile","description":"Mobile Work for CCC"}],"created":"2026-10-28T02:56:06.551-0400","description":"## Overview

Today each section of the job list is sorted by the linked CommCare app's lastAccessed, oldest first, so the opportunity you used least recently is at the top. Instead each section of the Connect job list should show the opportunity the worker most recently worked on first. This applies to all opportunities, not only PersonalID messaging ones.

## Implementation

Record the time a worker last taps any learn or delivery button (start learning, continue learning, claim, go to delivery, revisit learning, open a task) on an opportunity, keep it across syncs, and sort each job list section by it, newest first. Logging into a CommCare app directly no longer affects the order. Also remove the unused app-installed checks from the job list.

Spec: [Job list ordering](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#job-list-ordering), [Screens](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#screens)

## Acceptance Criteria

* Each job list section is ordered by last worked time, most recent first
* Tapping a learn or delivery button, or a task, moves that opportunity to the top of its section
* The order survives an opportunity sync

fields.description:
## Overview

Today each section of the job list is sorted by the linked CommCare app's lastAccessed, oldest first, so the opportunity you used least recently is at the top. Instead each section of the Connect job list should show the opportunity the worker most recently worked on first. This applies to all opportunities, not only PersonalID messaging ones.

## Implementation

Record the time a worker last taps any learn or delivery button (start learning, continue learning, claim, go to delivery, revisit learning, open a task) on an opportunity, keep it across syncs, and sort each job list section by it, newest first. Logging into a CommCare app directly no longer affects the order. Also remove the unused app-installed checks from the job list.

Spec: [Job list ordering](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#job-list-ordering), [Screens](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#screens)

## Acceptance Criteria

* Each job list section is ordered by last worked time, most recent first
* Tapping a learn or delivery button, or a task, moves that opportunity to the top of its section
* The order survives an opportunity sync

## Implementation

lastPrompt: another change - I would like to connect last worked date to the a new API property last_active  (will need server to expose it, it already has the data), so that we maintaint theordering even on fres…

content.text:
Keeping the newer of the two times has one catch: as the code stands, the server value would never win on a fresh sign-in. [Certain] The `ConnectJobRecord` constructor sets `lastWorkedDate = new Date()` (`ConnectJobRecord.java:194`), so a newly parsed job always has a device time of "now", which is later than any server timestamp. To fix this, the spec now has `fromJson` set `lastWorkedDate` from `last_active`, and to the epoch (1970) when `last_active` is absent or null. That also puts never-worked jobs below worked ones, rather than at the top with the time of the first sync.

**Spec changes (local only):**
- *Server contract:* adds `last_active` as a new nullable timestamp on every opportunity, not just messaging ones. It needs server work.
- *Job list ordering:*
  - `fromJson` reads `last_active`, and uses the epoch when it's missing.
  - `storeOrUpdateJob` keeps whichever of the stored and incoming `lastWorkedDate` is more recent.
  - Tapping a learn or delivery button still sets the time on the device.
  - Accepted risk: device clock and server clock are compared directly, so a device with a wrong clock can order jobs incorrectly.
  - `lastWorkedDate` is already a persisted column, so there's still no migration.

**CCCT-2994:**
- The description now covers the server value and the newer-wins rule, and notes that it depends on the server exposing `last_active`.
- It links the Server contract section.
- It has three new acceptance criteria:
  - The order follows the server on a fresh sign-in.
  - The device time is replaced only by a later server time.
  - Jobs with no last active time sort at the bottom.

No ticket covers exposing `last_active` on the server. Do you want me to create a web/server ticket under CCCT-2860 for it? The links still point to `c32ee32` until you push the spec.
